text:
Alex Support: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-retail) opened a high-priority ticket: after the 03:00 PDT rollout their assistant started returning much more 'creative' answers (hallucinations), previously concise. They say it started exactly after the deploy.

Alex Support: Quick symptom summary: deterministic prompts that used to be pinned to short factual replies are now verbose and inventing details. Examples attached by customer. They believe only the service changed, not their prompt.

Alex Support: Repro steps from customer: 1) POST /v1/generate 2) model: "redwood-7b-instruct@v2" 3) payload below:

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-7b-instruct@v2",
  "input": "List the top 3 shipping countries for orders placed in Q4. Keep to one line each.",
  "max_tokens": 60
}
```

Alex Support: Customer said response used to be like:
"1. US - 42%
2. CA - 18%
3. GB - 9%"
Now they see multi-paragraph explanation and invented percentages.

Priya Eng: tagging @Mark ML and @Carlos Ops — do we have any config changes that could affect sampling defaults or global request overrides in the last deploy? :thinking_face:

deploy-bot: Deployed release r2026.03.15-03 to production (canary->global) by ci/cd. Config diff: 
- routing.tier: stable -> staged
+ experiments.global_sampling_defaults: true
(release notes: "enable per-tenant sampling defaults rollout")

Mark ML: I saw that flag in the release. If global_sampling_defaults flips on, it can inject default sampling params at the gateway level when requests omit them. Might explain change.

Alex Support: Customer payload didn't include `temperature` or `top_p`. They assumed platform defaults would remain conservative. We should confirm what new defaults are.

Carlos Ops: Checking config secrets and rollout logs...
Carlos Ops: Found PR #842 merged this morning: "introduce global sampling defaults and rollout to prod". Canary shows default `temperature: 0.8`, `top_p: 1.0` for tenants without explicit sampling. That is definitely more stochastic than previous internal default (~0.2 / 0.9).

Priya Eng: Oof. That would cause the drift. Two action items: 1) immediate mitigation for affected tenants (revert or override to conservative defaults), 2) communicate to customers and CSMs. Also need a postmortem/rollout gating.

Alex Support: Customer asked for ETA to fix. They've paused the feature in their app while we investigate. Lisa, can you notify them and offer a retry when we have a fix?

Lisa CSM: On it. I'll message them with a temporary workaround: pass "temperature":0.2, "top_p":0.9 in the request until we fix. Will offer an apology and priority support.

Mark ML: Short-term hotfix: we can push a patch to the gateway to set tenant-defaults to previous conservative values for all tenants that didn't opt into the experiment. Carlos, can you revert the config flag for global rollout?

Carlos Ops: Preparing revert patch now. Rolling back experiment flag to false across prod nodes. I'll also add a targeted override for acme-retail to restore `temp=0.2/top_p=0.9` immediately.

Carlos Ops: rollback started at 1765553000 — will stream logs.

Alex Support: Customer notified (via Lisa). They've applied the manual override client-side for now but want platform fix.

deploy-bot: Rollback job rb-176555-1 completed at 1765553200. Config `experiments.global_sampling_defaults` set -> false. Tenant override created for acme-retail.

Mark ML: Can folks confirm a sample request from the customer now returns the old concise output? We should capture a golden prompt and compare token-level differences.

Alex Support: Customer just sent new response — looks back to expected format. They've validated a few cases.

Priya Eng: Great. Next: 1) postmortem and improved rollout gating for config flags that affect runtime inference params, 2) add automated smoke tests on a subset of tenants for sampling-sensitive prompts, 3) doc change to clarify platform default sampling values.

Lisa CSM: Customer is grateful for fast rollback. Asking for a change log and assurance this won't happen silently again. I'll collect their before/after examples for the postmortem.

Mark ML: I'll own the postmortem with Priya and Carlos. We'll include repro steps, PR timeline, canary checks, and required staging tests.

Alex Support: Adding note: customer mentioned some billing anomalies during the noisy period (spike in tokens). Might need billing support to reconcile overcharged burst.

Priya Eng: Noted. @finance-bot can you flag potential token spikes for acme-retail between 1765551200-1765553200?

Alex Support: Thanks everyone. Closing loop once postmortem and billing check are complete. :thumbsup:
